definitions.explanation: A free-reed wind instrument with 17 bamboo pipes mounted on a small cup-shaped chamber, used in {雅楽|ががく} (Japanese court music). Produces an ethereal, sustained chord.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}は{笙|しょう}を{吹|ふ}く。
{雅楽|ががく}では{笙|しょう}が{独特|どくとく}な{和音|わおん}を{奏|かな}でる。
examples.english: In gagaku the sho produces distinctive sustained chords.

examples.japanese: {笙|しょう}の{音色|ねいろ}は{天上|てんじょう}から{差|さ}し{込|こ}む{光|ひかり}にたとえられる。
examples.english: The tone of the sho is likened to light streaming down from the heavens.

notes:
A traditional wind instrument central to {雅楽|ががく} (Japanese court music). The 17 vertical bamboo pipes give it a distinctive shape resembling phoenix wings, and it is one of very few East Asian instruments that play chords. The player both inhales and exhales through the mouthpiece.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {笙|しょう}を{吹|ふ}く: to play the sho
- {笙|しょう}の{音色|ねいろ}: the tone of the sho
- {笙|しょう}{奏者|そうしゃ}: sho player

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {篳篥|ひちりき}: hichiriki, double-reed instrument used alongside the sho in gagaku
- {龍笛|りゅうてき}: ryuteki, transverse flute used in gagaku
